headline: Corn and beans break lower as harvest pressure builds
lead: Corn is at $4.74¼ overnight, down 4 cents, and beans are off 3¾ cents at $12.60½. China bought more US beans this week, its first cargoes since the Trump-Xi summit, but harvest supply is still winning. Every bushel coming out of the field right now is being sold into a market that already has plenty.
teaser: Corn and beans both break lower overnight even with fresh China bean purchases.

one_number.unit: soybean cargoes China booked this week
one_number.context: State-owned Chinese buyers booked at least 20 cargoes, the first purchases since the late-September Trump-Xi summit, and beans still fell.

sections.title: Corn and beans break lower
sections.body:
- Corn fell 4 cents to **$4.74¼** and beans gave back 3¾ cents to $12.60½, both still short of the next support levels traders are watching.
- China's fresh soybean buying, the first since the Trump-Xi summit, wasn't enough to hold the board up.
sections.so_what: Demand news is losing to the size of the crop coming out of the field.

sections.title: Cattle firm, feeders hold
sections.body:
- Live cattle gained 0.7% to **$227.52** on cash hopes, while feeders eked out a 0.2% gain to $343.98.
- Packing plant closures are leaving some feeders with fewer places to sell, even as the board holds up.
- Hogs sat flat at $75.55, no fresh news to move them either way.
sections.so_what: Cattle demand is steady, but where to sell is getting harder for some feeders.

sections.title: Crude holds near $99 on tanker risk
sections.body:
- WTI crude rose 1.3% to **$99.25**, with Brent reported stuck near $105 on more Iranian tanker attacks.
- The US put another 17 million barrels of SPR crude up for sale, a day after the IEA sped up its own emergency releases.
sections.so_what: Governments releasing reserves shows how tight fuel supply is right now.

outside_the_pit.title: Winter weather outlook webinar set for October 21
outside_the_pit.body: A live session on the winter temperature and precipitation outlook runs Wednesday, October 21 at 1 p.m. CT, useful for feed and pasture planning.

watch_list.desc: Export sales report. Another round of China bean bookings would say the demand story is real, not one-off.
Corn back under $4.70 or beans under $12.50 would confirm harvest supply is still setting the tone.
Crude holding above $99 keeps pressure on fuel and fertilizer costs into fall fieldwork.

source_summary: CME/CBOT settlement data, USDA, oilprice.com, farmpolicynews.illinois.edu, thefencepost.com, beefmagazine.com, feedstuffs.com, agweb.com

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $4.91 vs $4.62 projected (+6.3%), 12 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.83 vs $11.09 projected (+15.7%), 12 of 22 trading days in.
harvest_clock.note: Ours: the average of the daily CBOT settles through Oct 16, figured the way USDA RMA does. RMA posts corn at $4.93 and soybeans at $12.87, both through Oct 14. Window and projected price: USDA RMA, as of Oct 15. Oct 1-31 window, most states.

corrections.text: The hog price in this issue, $75.55, was the October contract, which expired Oct 14. December lean hogs settled at $66.925 on Oct 16, up 35 cents. Other prices here were afternoon trades read before the settle; the Oct 16 settles were corn $4.74¼ (down 3¾ cents), soybeans $12.61¼ (down 1¾ cents), wheat $6.60½ (down 9½ cents), live cattle $227.55 and feeder cattle $343.625. Crude oil's $99.25 was a 1:46 p.m. trade, not the close.
